messages:
maria: Heads-up — nightly evals flagged a sharp uptick in pset_23 failures after the promptset v23.1 push last night.
nightly-eval-bot: ALERT: pset_23 failure rate +18% vs baseline (window 00:00-06:00 UTC). Top diffs: negation, date-parsing, concise-answer scoring. See /evals/2026-03-19/pset_23/report.pdf
ajay: Is this the rebaseline that removed the explicit 'do not assume' phrasing?
sophie: yep, v23.1 removed a clarifying negative example to reduce redundancy. It was small but might shift model heuristics.
david: Which models/quant configs showed the spike? could be quantization sensitivity.
nightly-eval-bot: Breakdown: rdm-1-int8: +30% fail, rdm-1-fp16: +5% fail, rdm-2-int8: +22% fail. Regression appears larger on int8 runs.
qa-bot: Sampling of bad generations attached: 
```
Q: "Did the user not want the system to assume X?"
A (bad): "Yes, definitely assume X."
```
maria: that sample is a direct negation flip. Looks like prompt wording change increased negation hallucinations under quantized kernels.
ajay: Can someone run a quick local A/B using v23.0 vs v23.1 on rdm-1-int8 with 1000 seeds? I'll schedule a job.
sophie: I've started a canary: /jobs/5483. Early signal: repro rate ~28% under int8 with v23.1, vs 6% on v23.0.
david: That gap suggests the prompt change amplified rounding sensitivity. We should either revert the prompt or pin quant profile for rdm-1-int8 while we investigate.
maria: Ops — any concerns about rollback? it's a doc change but affects many downstream clients.
ops-oncall: rollback safe from infra side. Non-breaking. Do we have approval from policy?
ajay: Let's do temporary revert of v23.1 in the prompt registry, then queue a controlled rebaseline with more negative examples. Sophie + QA to approve.
sophie: I approve the revert. Will prepare a v23.2 that reintroduces one negative exemplar and adds a short guard: `Please do not infer facts not stated.`
qa-bot: Notify: QA will run rebaseline smoke: 2k samples across int8/fp16. Expect ~4h.
maria: ok doing revert now and kicking off the QA run. tagging @david for follow-up on quant kernels — can we add a test that exercises negation-heavy templates in the inference regression suite?
david: yes, I'll add a focused case to the nightly kernel stress tests.
ajay: After revert and QA pass, we should open a small experiment to see if a prompt rewrite (rather than revert) can keep conciseness while being quant-stable.
maria: thanks all. I'll post a follow-up with logs and the QA summary once the smoke completes. :thumbsup:
nightly-eval-bot: NOTE: incident created #INC-2026-042 for tracking.
